title: Linux
description: Learned the filesystem, permissions, process management, and enough shell to stop being afraid of a terminal with no GUI.
lessons: Everything is a file
chmod and chown solve more problems than you'd expect
systemd logs are your first debugging stop

title: Git
description: Version control as a way of thinking, not just a backup tool — branches, rebases, and the discipline of small commits.
lessons: Commit messages are documentation for future-me
Rebase locally, merge on shared branches
git bisect finds bugs faster than reading code

title: GitHub
description: Collaboration workflows — pull requests, code review, branch protection, and GitHub Actions as a first CI touchpoint.
lessons: Branch protection rules prevent 90% of accidental prod pushes
A good PR description saves a reviewer's whole afternoon

title: Docker
description: Containerizing applications — images, layers, volumes, and networking between containers.
lessons: Multi-stage builds keep images small
Named volumes beat bind mounts for data you care about
One process per container, mostly

title: Docker Compose
description: Orchestrating multi-container applications locally — the stepping stone before Kubernetes made sense.
lessons: depends_on doesn't mean 'wait until ready'
Environment files keep secrets out of compose.yml

title: Jenkins
description: Building CI pipelines from scratch — multibranch pipelines, quality gates, and artifact publishing.
lessons: Declarative pipelines age better than scripted ones
Quality gates only matter if they can actually block a merge

title: AWS
description: Core AWS services — EC2, IAM, S3, VPC, and security groups — enough to reason about a real cloud architecture.
lessons: IAM least privilege is worth the setup pain
Security groups are stateful, NACLs are not

title: Terraform
description: Infrastructure as code — writing reusable, parameterized modules instead of clicking through the AWS console.
lessons: State files are precious — lock them, back them up
Modules should read like documentation

title: Kubernetes
description: The core object model — Pods, Deployments, Services, ConfigMaps, Secrets — and how they fit together.
lessons: Declarative beats imperative once you have more than one replica
Liveness and readiness probes are not optional

title: RBAC
description: Role-based access control inside the cluster — Roles, RoleBindings, ServiceAccounts, and least-privilege by default.
lessons: Namespace-scoped roles beat cluster-wide ones almost every time
ServiceAccounts need the same scrutiny as human users

title: Ingress
description: Routing external traffic into the cluster with NGINX Ingress — hostnames, paths, and TLS termination.
lessons: Annotations do most of the heavy lifting in NGINX Ingress
One Ingress controller, many Ingress resources

title: Helm
description: Currently templating Kubernetes manifests into reusable charts instead of copy-pasting YAML between environments.
lessons: values.yaml is the real interface of a chart
Still learning: chart dependencies and subcharts

title: ArgoCD
description: Learning GitOps delivery — letting Git be the source of truth and ArgoCD reconcile the cluster to match it.
lessons: The reconciliation loop changes how you think about incidents
Still learning: app-of-apps patterns at scale

title: Prometheus
description: Learning metrics collection and PromQL to actually understand what a cluster is doing under load.
lessons: Cardinality is the silent killer of a Prometheus setup
Still learning: writing alerting rules that don't cause fatigue

title: Grafana
description: Turning Prometheus metrics into dashboards that answer real questions instead of just displaying numbers.
lessons: A dashboard should answer a question, not just show data
Still learning: templating dashboards across environments

title: What's Next
description: Service mesh fundamentals, deeper observability, and contributing back to an open-source DevOps project.
lessons: The learning loop doesn't stop — it just gets more specific
